summary: All nine task-intent criteria are met and verified against the worktree source and green gates. (1) Access-item nodes render their NAME via .vc-graph-card-label in both AccessNode branches; the RTL test asserts getByText for role/entitlement/AP labels. (2) The text status chip and all .vc-graph-status-chip* CSS are removed from the worktree — the only remaining references are the test's negative assertions (StatusChip/STATUS_CHIP absent; grep over src/ finds nothing but the 'is gone' check). (3) A three-state lower-right StatusIcon (AccessNode.tsx) uses distinct SVG shapes — hollow exclamation circle / check / hand-off arrow — with role=img + aria-label + <title> giving accessible names 'Needs review'/'Completed'/'Delegated', rendered only when data.reviewStatus is set; accessGraph stamps status solely on levels[1] (the user's directly-held item) and its user->item edge, so the user node, grid cards, deeper hops, and source carry no icon. (4) reviewStatusOf applies reassigned->delegated first (terminal even when also decided); union widened to needsReview|complete|delegated and a Record over it keeps the icon maps exhaustive. (5) isItemReviewed === reviewStatusOf(item)!=='needsReview' stays true for complete and delegated; metrics tests confirm dashboard counts invariant (reassigned counts as reviewed, not approved/revoked). (6) reviewStatus is excluded from rowKey/dedup; resolveMatrix keeps needsReview-wins with complete-vs-delegated resolving to delegated. (7) The delegated edge uses var(--vc-accent) with a distinct dotted '2 3' dash and no count badge. (8) The drill-down legend lists three entries and is drill-down-only. (9) npm run build (tsc -b + vite build) zero errors, npm run lint clean, npm test 31 files / 225 tests all green including the known useProvenance flake.
